Hi Elena / Carlos —

Thanks again for a great discovery call today. Quick recap and a proposed plan to get the POC (inference integration + observability) running smoothly: 

Summary of goals / success criteria (please confirm):
- Validate end-to-end latency and cost at target throughput (10 qps steady, 50 qps burst) with p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms for common prompts.
- Ensure visibility into regressions: per-prompt quality monitoring and alerts on model output drift (via sample prompt set).
- Verify reliability & fallback behavior under capacity stress (graceful fallback to smaller model variant).
- Export traces/logs/metrics to your monitoring stack for 30 days.

Observability plan (high-level):
- Dashboards: latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, error rates, model version comparisons, cache hit rate.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans for request lifecycle (ingest -> model -> response); sample traces for tail-latency events.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with request_id, model_version, prompt_hash, token_counts; deliver to S3 or your ELK.
- Metrics: per-route counters, histogram for token latency, GPU utilization, KV cache stats.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) Marcus and I share a dashboard spec + checklist (attached) — by Fri Jul 3.
2) Tech kickoff (30–45m) to validate data export (logs/traces/metrics) and S3/ELK permissions — propose Tue Jul 13.
3) POC run: 2–4 weeks after kickoff; mid-point review for preliminary results.
4) Final review demo and success validation.

Owners suggested:
- FintechX technical owner: Carlos Ruiz (confirm)
- Redwood SE: Marcus Lin
- Redwood AE / program owner: me (Marissa)
- CS observer: Naomi Feldman

Attachments: FintechX_POC_Observability_Checklist.xlsx, POC_Dashboard_Specs.pdf

Can you confirm the success criteria above and that Carlos will own the technical work on your side? If so we’ll lock the kickoff slot and circulate the workshop agenda.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Elena / Carlos —

Quick technical notes to complement Marissa’s checklist and to make the kickoff productive.

1) Dashboards (we’ll deliver Grafana JSON + Prometheus metrics):
   - Latency: request_latency_seconds histogram with p50/p95/p99 panels; separate by route/model_version.
   - Throughput: tokens_generated_total (counter) and requests_per_second (rate).
   - Errors: errors_total with labels (type=timeout|model_error|validation).
   - Cache: kv_cache_hit_ratio gauge, kv_cache_evictions_total.
   - Model quality: sampled_prompt_outputs (s3 pointer) + mismatch rate by prompt set.

2) Tracing & Logs:
   - Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans instrumented on all request lifecycle steps. Span tags: request_id, route, model_version, shard_id, gpu_id, seq_len.
   - Logs: structured JSON lines; required fields: timestamp, request_id, level, msg_type, model_version, prompt_hash, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms. We can push logs to your S3 (preferred) or a temporary ELK endpoint.

3) Exports / retention:
   - We can export metrics to Prometheus remote_write -> your Prometheus or Cortex.
   - Traces can be sampled (1% default) + adaptive sampling for tail latency events; full traces stored to your OTLP collector or S3 for the POC.
   - Retention: Redwood can keep 30 days by default; we can push/raw-export to your S3 for your 90-day requirement during POC.

4) Operational metrics & alerts (examples):
   - p95 request latency > 350ms for 1 minute -> page oncall
   - TPS drop > 30% vs baseline -> alert to platform team
   - Cache hit ratio < 60% -> warn and investigate prompt patterns
   - GPU utilization > 90% sustained for 5 minutes -> scale/burst policy

5) Data sampling & privacy:
   - We recommend sampling sensitive fields and hashing customer identifiers before export. We will work with Elena on the mapping.

Action items before kickoff (owners):
- Redwood: generate Grafana dashboards + Prometheus metric names (Marcus) — due Fri Jul 10.
- FintechX: confirm S3 bucket and IAM role for writes (Carlos) — due Tue Jul 7.
- Marissa: finalize kickoff agenda and workshop slate (Marissa) — due Mon Jul 6.

Happy to walk through a short tech pre-brief if you want — otherwise we’ll cover this at the kickoff.

Thanks,
